description: Proposed 20-claim calibration fixture. Claims are intentionally bounded so component-level support can be scored without allowing one supported noun to rescue an unsupported relationship.

claims.atomic_claim: Small geometric clay objects survive in several forms, and some bear incisions.
Catalogue object OIM A64678 is a broken clay envelope from Chogha Mish with tokens still inside.
Exterior marks on some hollow clay envelopes made enclosed quantities inspectable without immediately opening the envelope.
Seal impressions marked an association with authority, custody or witnessing.
In a representative manufacture workflow, an operator deposits counters, closes the envelope, marks and seals it, then lets it dry.
In a representative sealing workflow, an operator binds a closure, presses clay over it and rolls a seal; later access breaks the sealing.
Numerical tablet fragment ChM III-937a recorded the same transaction previously secured by hollow envelope OIM A64678.
Cylinder seals were used specifically to bind communal responsibility among Sumerian village elders.
Hollow clay bullae emerged specifically to prevent fraud during long-distance administration.
OIM A64678 was made because an administrator distrusted a shepherd delivering sheep.
Urban growth caused administrative memory to fail, and that failure directly caused the invention of clay tokens.
The need to break hollow envelopes to inspect their contents caused accountants to abandon envelopes and invent numerical tablets.
All hollow clay envelopes bear exterior impressions.
Geometric clay tokens formed one unified accounting code across 5,000 years.
Administrative recording followed an obligatory sequence from tokens to hollow envelopes to surface impressions to numerical tablets to proto-cuneiform.
Direct numerical recording on clay immediately and completely replaced envelopes and tokens.
Cylinder-seal impressions do not identify spoken syntax or linguistic phonology.
Uruk IV proto-cuneiform texts do not record running continuous spoken discourse, poetry, or historical narrative.
Reed tools likely produced the surviving rounded impressions and incised lines on Late Uruk clay.
Numerical information increasingly appeared directly on durable clay surfaces while older and parallel clay practices continued to overlap with direct surface recording.
